To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the folding/unfolding equilibrium of the juxta-membrane region of the phospholamban protein is correlated to its inhibition of the SERCA Ca2+ pump.
PLN conformation changes upon phosphorylation and lipid binding involve mostly the cytosolic region of PLN.
the conformation of phospholambin (PLN), an integral membrane protein, regulates the sarcoplasmatic reticulum Ca-ATPase (SR-ATPase) activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms underlying the regulation of the SERCA by PLN.
the structural and functional characterization of PLN in its native and phosphorylated states.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanism of PLN/SERCA regulation by the phosphorylation-dependent structural changes of PLN.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

PLN is in a dynamic state of equilibrium between a folded ground state (PLN T state) and a partially unfolded excited state (T' state), which is in turn regulated by the phosphorylation of PLNs Ser16.
the conformation of the PLN-SERCA complex is a key factor in the SERCA regulation.
the PLN conformation is a regulatory element for the SERCA pump.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PLN folding and unfolding are a key mechanism for SERCA regulation.
the regulation of SERCA by PLN involves a conformational switch between the folded (T) and unfolded (T') states of PLN.
PLN folding is required for inhibition of SERCA and unfolding of PLN is required for relief of SERCA inhibition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the regulation of the SERCA-PLN complex is a dynamic phenomenon that depends on PLN conformation.
the folding/unfolding transitions of PLN, which are triggered by the binding of phospholipids and Ca(2+), play a crucial role in SERCA regulation.
the conformation of PLN is the main regulatory mechanism for SERCa, and the population of the unfolded state (T') is linearly correlated with inhibition of SERCA.
